title: Ordering Schedule I and II Stock: DEA Form 222 and CSOS
topic: Controlled substance procurement / Schedule I and II ordering
subtopic: When an order is required, the 60-day window, defective and lost orders, and how each route is preserved
learning_objectives: State when a DEA Form 222 or a digitally signed electronic order is required for a Schedule I or II distribution, and name the movements 21 CFR 1305.03 excepts.
Read the 60-day window correctly: what it runs from, what it permits, and why it is not sixty business days.
Separate a defective order from a lost one, because the two failures have different cures and leave different records.
State how long each ordering record is kept, where it is kept, and what actually makes an electronic copy count as separately maintained.

Name the entries each side writes when a paper shipment moves: what the supplier records on the original, what the purchaser records on its copy when the containers arrive, and what a supplier outside ARCOS sends DEA.
Describe CSOS as the electronic equivalent of the paper form rather than a scan of one, and identify the duties that travel with the electronic route.
Name the report a purchaser owes when order forms are lost or stolen, and the one carve-out the regulation writes into it.

orientation.text: Ordering Schedule I and II stock is not dispensing, and the paperwork that governs it is not a prescription. 21 CFR 1305.03 attaches its requirement to a distribution: each distribution of a Schedule I or II controlled substance requires either a DEA Form 222 or its electronic equivalent under subpart C of part 1305 and part 1311. The document therefore sits between two registrants, a supplier and a purchasing pharmacy, and it records a movement of stock rather than a therapy decision. The regulation then lists the movements it does not reach, and the list is short and specific: distributions to persons exempted from registration, exports that conform with the Act, deliveries to a registered analytical laboratory or its DEA-approved agent, delivery from a central fill pharmacy to a retail pharmacy, deliveries to an authorized registrant by an ultimate user or by a long-term care facility on behalf of a resident or former resident or by a person authorized to dispose of a decedent's property, distributions to reverse distributors and distributors by collectors and law enforcement, and deliveries from ultimate users for a recall. Anything outside that list needs an order.

There are two routes to that order and they are alternatives, not a document and a copy of it. On the paper route the purchaser makes a copy of the original for its records and submits the original to the supplier, and 21 CFR 1305.13(a) lets that retained copy be in paper or electronic form. The purchaser keeps a copy of every executed form under 21 CFR 1305.17(a), together with copies of any unaccepted or defective forms and the statements attached to them, while 21 CFR 1305.17(b) puts the original on the other side of the transaction: the supplier retains the original of each DEA Form 222 that it has filled. That allocation is visible in the failure provisions too, since both 21 CFR 1305.15 and 21 CFR 1305.16 describe the supplier sending an original back to the purchaser. On the electronic route the purchaser signs an order with a digital signature DEA issued to the purchaser or the purchaser's agent under part 1311, and subpart C fixes the data the order must carry, including a nine-character tracking number the purchaser assigns in the format of the last two digits of the year, the letter X, and six characters of the purchaser's choosing. Scanning a completed paper form does not produce an electronic order, because an electronic order is valid only when it carries that DEA-issued digital signature.

Both routes run on the same sixty-day window, and it is sixty days rather than sixty business days. 21 CFR 1305.13(b) lets a supplier fill a paper order in part and supply the balance by additional shipments within 60 days following the date of the form, and states that no DEA Form 222 is valid more than 60 days after its execution by the purchaser, except as paragraph (f) of that section specifies for the Defense Supply Center. Subpart C sets the same window for an electronic order: it may be filled in part with the balance supplied within 60 days following the date of the order, and no order is valid more than 60 days after execution. The window is permission to finish an order already accepted, not permission to keep ordering, and once it closes the unshipped balance needs a new order rather than an extension. The same paragraph is also where the candidate learns that filling is discretionary: a supplier may fill the order if possible and if it desires to do so, and it records on the original its registration number where the purchaser has not entered it, the number of commercial or bulk containers furnished on each item, and the date the containers are shipped.

A paper order leaves entries on both sides once the goods move, and the paper route is not silent where the electronic route speaks. When the shipment arrives, 21 CFR 1305.13(e) requires the purchaser to record on its copy of the DEA Form 222 the number of commercial or bulk containers furnished on each item and the dates on which the containers are received, which is the paper counterpart of the record 21 CFR 1305.22(g) has a purchaser create and link electronically to a CSOS order. On the supplier's side 21 CFR 1305.13(d) requires the original to be retained for the supplier's files in accordance with 21 CFR 1305.17(c), and it adds a duty that catches a registrant who does not report acquisition and disposition transactions to ARCOS, such as a practitioner: that supplier must make and submit a copy of the original DEA Form 222 to DEA, forwarded at the close of the month during which the order is filled, or, where the order is filled by partial shipments, at the close of the month during which the final shipment is made or the 60-day validity period expires. A pharmacy can reach those supplier duties, because 21 CFR 1305.06 lets a purchaser who obtained a Schedule I or II substance on an order return it to the supplier of the substance with a DEA Form 222 or electronic order from that supplier, and lets a person registered to dispense Schedule II substances distribute them to another dispenser on an order in the circumstances 21 CFR 1307.11 describes. In either movement the pharmacy is the party filling the order.

A defective order and a lost order are different failures with different cures, and questions are built on the seam between them. Under 21 CFR 1305.15 a paper form must not be filled if the order is not complete, legible, or properly prepared, executed or endorsed, or if it shows any alteration, erasure or change of any description; the supplier returns the original to the purchaser with a statement of the reason, the purchaser files both, and the section says in terms that a defective form may not be corrected and must be replaced by a new form before the order can be filled. Initialling an altered line, rewriting a quantity, or asking the supplier to fix the entry are three spellings of the same wrong answer, and subpart C reaches the same result electronically by providing that neither purchaser nor supplier may correct a defective order and that the purchaser must issue a new one. A lost form is not defective at all: under 21 CFR 1305.16 a purchaser who ascertains that an unfilled form has been lost executes another and attaches a statement giving the order form number and date of the lost form and stating that the goods it covered were not received through its loss.

Retention is where the two routes look most alike and behave least alike, so read which rule a question is standing on. 21 CFR 1305.17(c) requires DEA Forms 222 to be maintained separately from all other records of the registrant and kept available for inspection for two years, and a purchaser with several registered locations keeps the executed copy and its attachments at the registered location printed on the form, though unexecuted forms are outside that sentence and may be kept elsewhere under 21 CFR 1305.12(e). The electronic half of the rule is the half candidates misread. 21 CFR 1305.17(e) does not demand a separate filing cabinet: it deems electronic copies of Forms 222 to be maintained separately if they are readily retrievable separately from all other records, and readily retrievable is a defined term. Under 21 CFR 1300.01(b) it means records kept by automatic data processing systems or other electronic or mechanized recordkeeping systems in such a manner that they can be separated out from all other records in a reasonable time, or records on which certain items are asterisked, redlined or otherwise visually identifiable apart from other items. The test is therefore what the system can produce, not where the file physically sits, and the same paragraph lets the copies live on a system at a location different from the registered location so long as they are readily retrievable at the registered location. Electronic orders are preserved under subpart C's own provision rather than by cross-reference to the Form 222 rule: for each order filled the purchaser retains the original signed order and all linked records for two years, along with copies of every unaccepted or defective order and each linked statement, the supplier retains its original and linked records for two years, and records held on a central server must be readily retrievable at the registered location.

Fillable in part with the balance within 60 days following the date of the order; no order valid more than 60 days after execution

The purchaser executes another form and attaches a statement giving the lost form's order form number and date and stating the goods were not received (21 CFR 1305.16)

Who keeps what

A copy of each filled electronic order, or a DEA-specified electronic report of it, within two business days (21 CFR 1305.29)

Two years on both sides under subpart C's own preservation provision, with central-server records readily retrievable at the registered location

worked_examples.scenario: A supplier telephones on day 64 after your pharmacy executed a paper DEA Form 222 and offers to ship the two line items it could not supply on the first shipment. Your technician counts that only about forty-five working days have passed and asks whether the balance can still go out on the original form, since the shortfall was the supplier's back order rather than anything the pharmacy did.
steps: Identify which clock the facts are asking about. This is the 60-day window in 21 CFR 1305.13(b), which governs both the validity of the form and the period for shipping the balance of a partly filled order.

Read the unit. The paragraph says 60 days following the date of the form, and no more than 60 days after execution by the purchaser. It says days, not business days, so the technician's count of working days is not the count the regulation uses.

Fix the start point. The window runs from the purchaser's execution of the form, and neither a supplier, a purchaser nor a back order moves that date; the single exception the paragraph carries, in 21 CFR 1305.13(f), is for Defense Supply Center procurement officers and does not reach a retail pharmacy.
Decide what happens to the unshipped balance. The window has closed, so the balance does not ship on the expired form; a fresh order is what puts those line items back in play.
worked_examples.resolution: The balance may not be shipped on the original form. The error the scenario invites is reading the 60 days as 60 business days, which would still be running on day 64; the second error is treating a supplier back order as something that extends a form the regulation makes invalid by its own terms.

worked_examples.scenario: A paper DEA Form 222 reaches the supplier on day 20 after execution. The form is well inside its validity period, but the purchaser wrote over one Schedule II quantity after signing. The purchaser offers to initial the change so the order can ship today rather than wait for a replacement, and points out that there is still more than a month left on the form.
steps: Split the two questions. Timeliness lives in 21 CFR 1305.13(b) and defect lives in 21 CFR 1305.15, and a form can satisfy one while failing the other.
Apply the defect test. An order showing any alteration, erasure or change of any description must not be filled, and writing over a signed quantity is exactly such a change.

Ask whether the defect can be cured. The section says a defective DEA Form 222 may not be corrected and must be replaced by a new form for the order to be filled, so an initial from the purchaser cures nothing.

Follow the routing the regulation sets. The supplier returns the original to the purchaser with a statement as to the reason, and the purchaser keeps the returned original and the statement in its files.
worked_examples.resolution: The order does not ship on this form; the purchaser executes a replacement. The error the scenario invites is letting a healthy 60-day clock stand in for validity, as though a form still inside its window could not also be one the supplier is forbidden to fill.

worked_examples.scenario: Your pharmacy mailed an executed paper DEA Form 222 to its supplier three weeks ago. The supplier says the form never arrived and that no Schedule II goods were shipped, and the pharmacy cannot produce the original. The stock is still needed, and a colleague suggests faxing the supplier the retained copy so the order can be filled from that instead.
steps: Name the failure. The form is unfilled and lost, not defective, so 21 CFR 1305.16 rather than 21 CFR 1305.15 supplies the procedure.

Execute a replacement. The purchaser executes another DEA Form 222 and attaches a statement containing the order form number and date of the lost form and stating that the goods it covered were not received through the loss of that form.

Place the copies where the regulation puts them. A copy of the second form and a copy of the statement are retained with a copy of the first form, and a copy of the statement goes to the supplier attached to a copy of the second form.

Plan for the original resurfacing. If the supplier to whom the first form was directed later receives it, the supplier marks 'Not accepted' upon the face and returns the original to the purchaser, who attaches it to the statement.

Read the reporting paragraph before adding a report. The immediate report of a lost or stolen order form, made with the serial number of each form to the Special Agent in Charge of the DEA divisional office for the registrant's area, is written for used or unused forms lost or stolen other than in the course of transmission, and this form went missing in transmission.
worked_examples.resolution: The regulation's answer to a lost unfilled form is a freshly executed form with the required statement attached, not the retained copy. The error the scenario invites is treating the retained copy as a substitute original; the subtler error is reaching for the immediate loss report without reading the carve-out the paragraph writes into it.

worked_examples.scenario: A pharmacy keeps electronic copies of its executed DEA Forms 222 in the same document system it uses for invoices and delivery notes; the system indexes each document by type and can list and export every Form 222 on demand. The pharmacy also keeps that system on a server at the chain's head office in another state. Beside it, a second pharmacy files its paper Forms 222 loose in the general invoice binder. The manager asks whether any of this is a problem, and whether CSOS orders can be filed the same way.
steps: Start with what the paper rule requires. 21 CFR 1305.17(c) requires DEA Forms 222 to be maintained separately from all other records of the registrant and kept available for inspection for two years, which is why the second pharmacy's loose filing in the invoice binder fails.

Read the deeming rule for electronic copies rather than importing the paper one. 21 CFR 1305.17(e) deems electronic copies to be maintained separately if they are readily retrievable separately from all other records, so sharing a system with other records is not itself the defect.

Apply the defined term. Under 21 CFR 1300.01(b) readily retrievable means the records are kept by an electronic or mechanized recordkeeping system in such a manner that they can be separated out from all other records in a reasonable time, so a system that can pull every Form 222 out on demand satisfies the test even though invoices sit beside them.

Apply the off-site rule to the head-office server. Electronic copies may be stored on a system at a location different from the registered location, provided they are readily retrievable at the registered location.

Answer the CSOS half on its own provision. Electronic orders are preserved under subpart C, which requires the purchaser to retain each original signed order and all linked records for two years and requires central-server records to be readily retrievable at the registered location.
worked_examples.resolution: The first pharmacy is compliant on both counts: a shared electronic system is acceptable because the Forms 222 can be separated out in a reasonable time, and the head-office server is acceptable because retrieval at the registered location works. The second pharmacy's loose paper filing is not, because paper forms must be maintained separately from all other records. The error the scenario invites is reading 21 CFR 1305.17(e) as a rule about where an electronic copy is stored, when the defined term makes it a rule about what the system can produce; the second error is assuming the Form 222 preservation rule is also the rule for CSOS orders.

worked_examples.scenario: A supplier's van delivers against a paper DEA Form 222 the pharmacy executed three weeks ago, bringing four of the six line items. The technician checks the cartons against the packing slip, files the delivery note with the invoices and puts the pharmacy's copy of the form back in the Form 222 file untouched, on the view that the supplier has already written the shipping entries on the original it kept.
steps: Separate the two sets of entries. 21 CFR 1305.13(b) is about what the supplier records on the original: its registration number where the purchaser has not entered it, the number of commercial or bulk containers furnished on each item, and the date the containers are shipped.

Read the purchaser's own paragraph. 21 CFR 1305.13(e) requires the purchaser to record on its copy of the DEA Form 222 the number of commercial or bulk containers furnished on each item and the dates on which the containers are received by the purchaser, so the pharmacy's copy does not stay untouched.

Notice that the two shipments are two receipt dates. Because the order was filled in part, the balance may still arrive within 60 days following the date of the form, and the paragraph asks for the dates on which containers are received rather than a single date.

Check the electronic counterpart so the duty is not mistaken for a CSOS feature. On the electronic route 21 CFR 1305.22(g) has the purchaser create a record of the quantity of each item received and the date received, electronically linked to the original order and archived.
worked_examples.resolution: The pharmacy writes the containers received and the date of receipt on its own copy of the form, and does so again when the balance arrives. The error the scenario invites is treating the supplier's entries on the original as the whole of the paperwork, which leaves the purchaser's copy with no record that the goods ever arrived.

retrieval_prompts.prompt: What does 21 CFR 1305.03 attach the order requirement to, and what are the two acceptable instruments?
retrieval_prompts.answer: Each distribution of a Schedule I or II controlled substance; either a DEA Form 222 or its electronic equivalent under subpart C of part 1305 and part 1311.

retrieval_prompts.prompt: Name three movements 21 CFR 1305.03 excepts from the order requirement.
retrieval_prompts.answer: Any three of: distributions to persons exempted from registration; conforming exports; deliveries to a registered analytical laboratory or its DEA-approved agent; delivery from a central fill pharmacy to a retail pharmacy; deliveries to an authorized registrant by an ultimate user, by a long-term care facility on behalf of a resident or former resident, or by a person authorized to dispose of a decedent's property; distributions to reverse distributors and distributors by collectors and law enforcement; and deliveries from ultimate users for a recall.

retrieval_prompts.prompt: Sixty days from what event, and sixty days of which kind?
retrieval_prompts.answer: Sixty calendar days from the purchaser's execution of the form; the same window bounds the supplier's shipment of the balance of a partly filled order.

retrieval_prompts.prompt: A supplier is asked to initial an altered quantity on an otherwise timely Form 222. What does 21 CFR 1305.15 require?
retrieval_prompts.answer: The form must not be filled; the supplier returns the original with a statement as to the reason, and the defective form may not be corrected but must be replaced by a new form for the order to be filled.

retrieval_prompts.prompt: What two things must the statement attached to a replacement Form 222 contain after a loss?
retrieval_prompts.answer: The order form number and date of the lost form, and a statement that the goods it covered were not received through the loss of that form.

retrieval_prompts.prompt: Which losses of order forms trigger the immediate report, to whom, and which losses are carved out?
retrieval_prompts.answer: Theft or loss of used or unused forms by a purchaser or supplier triggers an immediate report on discovery, stating the serial number of each form, to the Special Agent in Charge of the DEA divisional office responsible for the registrant's area; losses in the course of transmission are carved out of that paragraph.

retrieval_prompts.prompt: An electronic copy of a Form 222 sits on a system that also holds invoices. What decides whether 21 CFR 1305.17(e) is satisfied?
retrieval_prompts.answer: Whether the copies are readily retrievable separately from all other records. Sharing a system is not the test; under 21 CFR 1300.01(b) the question is whether the recordkeeping system can separate the Forms 222 out from all other records in a reasonable time.

retrieval_prompts.prompt: State the definition of readily retrievable that 21 CFR 1300.01(b) supplies.
retrieval_prompts.answer: Records kept by automatic data processing systems or other electronic or mechanized recordkeeping systems in such a manner that they can be separated out from all other records in a reasonable time, and/or records on which certain items are asterisked, redlined, or in some other manner visually identifiable apart from other items appearing on the records.

retrieval_prompts.prompt: What does the purchaser write on its own copy of a paper DEA Form 222, and when?
retrieval_prompts.answer: The number of commercial or bulk containers furnished on each item and the dates on which the containers are received by the purchaser, under 21 CFR 1305.13(e).

retrieval_prompts.prompt: Who keeps the original of a filled paper DEA Form 222, and which suppliers must also send DEA a copy of it?
retrieval_prompts.answer: The supplier retains the original of each form it has filled under 21 CFR 1305.17(b). A supplier that is not required to report to ARCOS, such as a practitioner, must also submit a copy to DEA at the close of the month during which the order is filled, or, for partial shipments, at the close of the month of the final shipment or of the 60-day expiry.

retrieval_prompts.prompt: How long is an electronic order kept, by whom, and what does the rule add for a central server?
retrieval_prompts.answer: Two years by the purchaser, covering the original signed order and all linked records for each order filled plus copies of unaccepted or defective orders and their linked statements, and two years by the supplier; records on a central server must be readily retrievable at the registered location.

retrieval_prompts.prompt: What must a CSOS order carry that a paper form does not, and what may it contain besides Schedule II items?
retrieval_prompts.answer: A digital signature DEA issued to the purchaser or the purchaser's agent, and a nine-character purchaser-assigned tracking number formed from the last two digits of the year, the letter X, and six characters of the purchaser's choosing; the order may also include substances outside Schedules I and II and non-controlled substances.

retrieval_prompts.prompt: Within what period must a supplier report a filled electronic order to DEA?
retrieval_prompts.answer: Two business days, forwarding either a copy of the electronic order or an electronic report of it in a format DEA specifies.

quick_review.text: Either a DEA Form 222 or its electronic equivalent under subpart C of part 1305 and part 1311 is required for each distribution of a Schedule I or II controlled substance, subject only to the movements 21 CFR 1305.03 excepts.

Those exceptions include delivery from a central fill pharmacy to a retail pharmacy and deliveries to an authorized registrant by an ultimate user or by a long-term care facility on behalf of a resident or former resident.

21 CFR 1305.13(b) permits partial filling with the balance supplied within 60 days following the date of the form, and makes no DEA Form 222 valid more than 60 days after its execution by the purchaser.

The same paragraph leaves filling to the supplier's discretion, and requires the supplier to record on the original its registration number where the purchaser has not entered it, the number of commercial or bulk containers furnished on each item, and the date the containers are shipped.
A DEA Form 222 must not be filled if the order is not complete, legible, or properly prepared, executed or endorsed, or if it shows any alteration, erasure or change of any description.
A defective DEA Form 222 may not be corrected; it must be replaced by a new form for the order to be filled, and the supplier returns the original to the purchaser with a statement as to the reason.
A lost unfilled DEA Form 222 is answered by executing another form with a statement giving the lost form's order form number and date and confirming that the goods it covered were not received.

Theft or loss of used or unused DEA Forms 222, other than in the course of transmission, is reported immediately upon discovery, stating the serial number of each form, to the Special Agent in Charge of the DEA divisional office responsible for the registrant's area.

DEA Forms 222 are maintained separately from all other records of the registrant and kept available for inspection for two years, and a purchaser with several registered locations keeps the executed copy and its attachments at the registered location printed on the form; unexecuted forms are excluded from that sentence and may be kept elsewhere under 21 CFR 1305.12(e).

Electronic copies of Forms 222 are deemed separately maintained if readily retrievable separately from all other records, and may be stored at another location provided they are readily retrievable at the registered location.

Readily retrievable is defined in 21 CFR 1300.01(b) as records kept by automatic data processing or other electronic or mechanized recordkeeping systems in such a manner that they can be separated out from all other records in a reasonable time, or records on which items are asterisked, redlined or otherwise visually identifiable apart from other items, so an electronic copy that shares a system with other records can still satisfy 21 CFR 1305.17(e).
The purchaser records on its copy of the DEA Form 222 the number of commercial or bulk containers furnished on each item and the dates on which the containers are received by the purchaser.

The supplier retains the original of each DEA Form 222 it has filled, and a supplier that is not required to report acquisition and disposition transactions to ARCOS, such as a practitioner, also submits a copy of the original to DEA at the close of the month during which the order is filled, or of the month of the final partial shipment or of the 60-day expiry.

A pharmacy can find itself on the supplier's side of an order form: 21 CFR 1305.06 lets a purchaser return a Schedule I or II substance to the supplier of that substance on an order from the supplier, and lets a dispenser distribute Schedule II substances to another dispenser on an order in the circumstances 21 CFR 1307.11 describes.
An electronic order is valid only if signed with a digital signature DEA issued to the purchaser or the purchaser's agent under part 1311, and it must carry the data fields subpart C lists.
A supplier may not endorse an electronic order to another supplier to fill, and a defective electronic order may not be corrected by either side; the purchaser issues a new order.

On receiving a shipment against an electronic order the purchaser creates a record of the quantity of each item received and the date received, electronically linked to the original order and archived.

decision_logic.condition: Schedule I or II stock is being distributed to the pharmacy.
decision_logic.action: Require a DEA Form 222 or a digitally signed electronic order unless the movement is one 21 CFR 1305.03 excepts, such as delivery from a central fill pharmacy to a retail pharmacy.

decision_logic.condition: The pharmacy is choosing between the paper and the electronic route.
decision_logic.action: Treat them as alternatives rather than as an original and a copy: a scan of a completed Form 222 is not an electronic order, because an electronic order must be signed with a DEA-issued digital signature and carry the fields subpart C lists.

decision_logic.condition: A supplier proposes to ship the balance of a partly filled order.
decision_logic.action: Count 60 calendar days from the purchaser's execution. Inside the window the balance may go; outside it the order is no longer valid and a new order is needed.

decision_logic.condition: The order in hand is incomplete, illegible, improperly prepared or executed, altered or erased.
decision_logic.action: Do not fill it and do not correct it. On the paper route the original goes back to the purchaser with a statement as to the reason; on either route the purchaser executes a new order.

decision_logic.condition: An unfilled order cannot be produced and the goods were never received.
decision_logic.action: Execute another order and attach the statement 21 CFR 1305.16 requires; on the electronic route give the supplier a signed statement carrying the lost order's tracking number and date and link the replacement and the statement to the record of the first order.

decision_logic.condition: Order forms are found to be missing from the pharmacy's stock of blanks.
decision_logic.action: Report the loss immediately upon discovery, stating the serial number of each form, to the Special Agent in Charge of the DEA divisional office for the area, and notify that office at once if a form is later recovered or found.

decision_logic.condition: Ordering records are being filed, scanned or migrated to a new system.
decision_logic.action: Keep paper Forms 222 separate from all other records and available for inspection for two years; for an electronic copy ask whether the system can separate the Forms 222 out from all other records in a reasonable time, since that is what readily retrievable separately means, and not whether they share a store with other documents; preserve electronic orders and their linked records for two years under subpart C rather than under the Form 222 rule.

decision_logic.condition: A shipment arrives against a paper DEA Form 222, in whole or in part.
decision_logic.action: Write on the pharmacy's own copy the number of commercial or bulk containers furnished on each item and the date the containers were received, and repeat the entry for each later shipment inside the 60-day window.

decision_logic.condition: The pharmacy is the party filling a paper order rather than the party placing it.
decision_logic.action: Take the supplier's duties: retain the original of the form filled, and, because a pharmacy does not report to ARCOS, submit a copy of that original to DEA at the close of the month in which the order is filled or of the month of the final shipment or 60-day expiry.

exceptions.text: 21 CFR 1305.03 excepts seven movements from the order requirement: distributions to persons exempted from registration, conforming exports, deliveries to a registered analytical laboratory or its DEA-approved agent, delivery from a central fill pharmacy to a retail pharmacy, deliveries to an authorized registrant by an ultimate user or by a long-term care facility on behalf of a resident or former resident or by a person authorized to dispose of a decedent's property, distributions to reverse distributors and distributors by collectors and law enforcement, and deliveries from ultimate users for a recall.

21 CFR 1305.13(b) states the 60-day limit subject to an exception in paragraph (f) of the same section, under which registered procurement officers of the Defense Supply Center of the Defense Logistics Agency may take partial shipments over a period not exceeding six months and at locations other than the one printed on the form.
Subpart C carries the same Defense Supply Center exception for electronic orders, allowing shipment to other locations and partial shipments over a period not exceeding six months.

The immediate theft-or-loss report is written for used or unused forms lost or stolen other than in the course of transmission, so a form that goes missing on its way to the supplier is handled by the replacement-and-statement route instead.
An electronic order may include controlled substances outside Schedules I and II as well as non-controlled substances.

timing_deadlines.event: Validity of a paper DEA Form 222
timing_deadlines.timeframe: 60 days after its execution by the purchaser
timing_deadlines.consequence: Once the window closes the form is no longer valid and the unshipped balance requires a new order.

timing_deadlines.event: Balance of a partly filled paper order
timing_deadlines.timeframe: Within 60 days following the date of the DEA Form 222
timing_deadlines.consequence: Additional shipments inside the window complete the original order; outside it they do not.

timing_deadlines.event: Validity and partial shipment of a CSOS electronic order
timing_deadlines.timeframe: 60 days after execution by the purchaser
timing_deadlines.consequence: Subpart C sets the same window for the electronic route, so switching routes buys no extra time.
Forms are kept available for inspection for that period and maintained separately from all other records of the registrant.

timing_deadlines.event: Preservation of electronic orders and their linked records
timing_deadlines.consequence: Kept by the purchaser and by the supplier under subpart C's own preservation provision rather than the Form 222 rule.

timing_deadlines.event: Supplier's report to DEA of a filled electronic order
timing_deadlines.consequence: The supplier forwards a copy of the order or an electronic report of it in a format DEA specifies.

timing_deadlines.event: Copy of a filled paper DEA Form 222 sent to DEA by a supplier that does not report to ARCOS
timing_deadlines.timeframe: At the close of the month during which the order is filled, or, for partial shipments, at the close of the month during which the final shipment is made or the 60-day validity period expires
timing_deadlines.consequence: The duty falls on the party filling the order, so a pharmacy meets it when it is the supplier on a form rather than the purchaser.

timing_deadlines.event: Purchaser's receipt entries on its copy of a paper DEA Form 222
timing_deadlines.timeframe: On receipt of the containers, recording the dates they are received
timing_deadlines.consequence: Each shipment against the form adds its own entry, so a partly filled order produces more than one receipt date on the copy.

timing_deadlines.event: Theft or loss of used or unused DEA Forms 222
timing_deadlines.consequence: Reported with the serial number of each form to the Special Agent in Charge of the DEA divisional office responsible for the registrant's area.

timing_deadlines.event: Recovery of an unused form previously reported lost or stolen
timing_deadlines.consequence: The same Special Agent in Charge must be notified that the form has been recovered or found.

forms_records.text: The purchaser retains a copy of each executed DEA Form 222 and all copies of unaccepted or defective forms with each statement attached.
DEA Forms 222 are maintained separately from all other records of the registrant and kept available for inspection for two years.

A purchaser with several registered locations keeps the executed copy and any attached statements or related documents at the registered location printed on the form; the same sentence excludes unexecuted DEA Forms 222, which may be kept elsewhere under 21 CFR 1305.12(e).
The supplier retains the original of each DEA Form 222 that it has filled, under 21 CFR 1305.17(b).

Electronic copies of Forms 222 are deemed separately maintained if readily retrievable separately from all other records, and may be stored on a system at a location different from the registered location provided they are readily retrievable at the registered location.

The test in that deeming rule is the defined term in 21 CFR 1300.01(b): whether the recordkeeping system can separate the Forms 222 out from all other records in a reasonable time, or the items are visually identifiable apart from other items on the record.
When a form is not accepted or is defective, the supplier returns the original with a statement as to the reason and the purchaser retains the original and the statement in its files.

After a lost unfilled form, a copy of the second form and a copy of the statement are retained with a copy of the first form, and a copy of the statement is attached to the copy of the second form sent to the supplier.

On the paper route the supplier records on the original its DEA registration number where the purchaser has not entered it, the number of commercial or bulk containers furnished on each item, and the date the containers are shipped.

The purchaser records on its own copy of the paper form the number of commercial or bulk containers furnished on each item and the dates on which the containers are received, so the paper route has a receipt record of its own rather than only an electronic one.

A supplier that is not required to report acquisition and disposition transactions to ARCOS, such as a practitioner, submits a copy of the original paper form to DEA at the close of the month during which the order is filled, or, for partial shipments, at the close of the month during which the final shipment is made or the 60-day validity period expires.

For each electronic order filled the purchaser retains the original signed order and all linked records for two years, together with copies of every unaccepted or defective order and each linked statement, and the supplier retains each original order filled and its linked records for two years.
On receiving a shipment against an electronic order the purchaser records the quantity of each item received and the date received, electronically linked to the original order and archived.

role_duties.duty: Execute a DEA Form 222 or a digitally signed electronic order for each Schedule I or II distribution that is not within an exception in 21 CFR 1305.03.
Replace rather than repair: execute a new order when the one in hand is defective, and execute another with the required statement when an unfilled order is lost.
Report the theft or loss of used or unused order forms immediately upon discovery with the serial number of each form, and notify the same office if a form is later recovered.

Record on its copy of the paper form the number of commercial or bulk containers furnished on each item and the dates the containers are received, and create the linked electronic receipt record where the order was placed through CSOS.

Keep Forms 222 separately from all other records and available for inspection for two years, judging an electronic copy by whether it is readily retrievable separately, and keep electronic orders and their linked records for two years under subpart C.

Fill only an order that is complete, legible and unaltered, return a defective or unaccepted original to the purchaser with a statement as to the reason, and record the containers furnished and the shipping date on the original paper form.

Retain the original of each DEA Form 222 it has filled and, where it does not report acquisition and disposition transactions to ARCOS, submit a copy of that original to DEA at the close of the month in which the order is filled or, for partial shipments, of the month of the final shipment or of the 60-day expiry.

role_duties.role: Pharmacy filling an order rather than placing one
role_duties.duty: Recognise that it is the supplier, and takes on the supplier's duties, when it returns a Schedule I or II substance to the supplier it obtained it from or distributes Schedule II stock to another dispenser in the circumstances 21 CFR 1307.11 describes.

Forward a copy of each filled electronic order, or a DEA-specified electronic report of it, to DEA within two business days, and retain each original order filled with its linked records for two years.

common_traps.text: Reading the 60-day window as 60 business days, which keeps a form alive on day 64 that the regulation made invalid on day 61.
Letting a healthy 60-day clock stand in for validity, so an altered form still inside its window looks fillable.
Curing a defect by initialling the change, rewriting the quantity, or asking the supplier to correct the entry, when the regulation says a defective form may not be corrected and must be replaced.
Treating a lost order as a defective one, or a defective one as a loss, and so producing the wrong statement and the wrong file.
Attaching the immediate theft-or-loss report to a form that went missing on its way to the supplier, when the paragraph carves losses in the course of transmission out of that duty.

Turning the deeming rule in 21 CFR 1305.17(e) into a storage-segregation rule, and so answering that an electronic copy sharing a system with other records fails, when 21 CFR 1300.01(b) makes the test whether the system can separate the Forms 222 out in a reasonable time.

Running the deeming rule the other way and letting it excuse loose paper filing, when 21 CFR 1305.17(e) reaches electronic copies and paper forms are still maintained separately from all other records.
Treating the receipt record as a CSOS feature, when 21 CFR 1305.13(e) puts containers received and dates of receipt on the purchaser's copy of a paper form as well.
Assuming the paper route gives the supplier no duty to DEA and no retention duty, when the supplier keeps the original and a supplier outside ARCOS forwards DEA a copy at the close of the month.
Treating a scan of a completed paper form as an electronic order, when an electronic order must be signed with a DEA-issued digital signature and carry the fields subpart C lists.
Applying the Form 222 preservation rule to CSOS orders, when subpart C states the electronic retention duty in its own terms.
Confusing an order with a dispensing record: the requirement attaches to a distribution between registrants, not to filling a patient's prescription.
